objectives.text: Stay inside the Western security order while rearming from the bottom of the NATO table: the Strategic Vision 2025 (approved 18 Jul 2025) sets the budget at 2% of GDP in 2025 (EUR 12.8bn, up from 1.29% in 2024), rising to EUR 21.3bn in 2034, 11 more F-35s (45 in all), NASAMS air defence and a third frigate. In July 2026 Francken committed to hold 2% until 2029 and to draw a roadmap to the NATO 3.5% core target, which he calls 'particularly difficult' in the current budget climate; the government also counts 'resilience' spending (railways, cyber) to claim a total of about 3.4%.

grand_strategy.reading:
Belgium is a small power whose geography made it a host: the seat of the European
institutions and of NATO, the port of Antwerp, and the Euroclear depository that
keeps the greater part of Russia's frozen reserves. Its grand strategy is the
strategy of a host that must stay useful to everyone who matters and exposed to
none of them. That works while the host's guests agree; in 2025-26 they stopped
agreeing, and the host has been made to choose in public. The Euroclear file is the
clearest case in Luttwak's terms: a defensive refusal, motivated by fear of
liability, which gave Belgium the opposite of what it wanted (the loss of
influence among partners, a Russian pressure campaign that no EU decision
has lifted, and an indefinite freezing it can no longer veto).

The second thread is a late and under-funded rearmament. The F-35 decision, the
NASAMS purchase and the French nuclear-deterrence opening all point the same way,
but the 2% is a floor and the 3.5% an unfunded promise, and the F-35 delivery
schedule holds back the F-16s promised to Kyiv. The third is the empire's
afterimage: in Congo, Rwanda and Burundi Belgium speaks with moral authority and
little leverage, and each time it has used the one (sanctions, a public stance)
it has paid in the other. Non-events matter here: Belgium sent one officer, not
troops, to Greenland (January 2026) and did not join the eight NATO states hit by
Trump's tariff threat; it signed the New York Declaration on Palestine and has not
yet signed the decree.

stances_toward.note: The rival that holds the money: about EUR 185bn of the Bank of Russia's EUR 210bn immobilised in the EU sits at Euroclear in Brussels, frozen indefinitely by qualified majority since 12 Dec 2025, and Moscow's answer went through Belgium - the ambassador's threat of 'severe retaliation' (15 Nov 2025), the central bank's suit in the Moscow Arbitration Court (12 Dec 2025, won on 15 May 2026, appeal lost by Euroclear on 16 Jul), judgments the EU does not recognise. The November 2025 drones over Brussels, Liege and the air bases are suspected, not attributed. Rival, not adversary: Moscow wants its reserves and Belgium's veto on the reparations loan, which De Wever has so far supplied, not the end of the Belgian state; Belgium's own aim is Euroclear's protection. Cooling with every judgment. Bond - none.

relations_from.summary: On 3 Mar 2026 De Wever confirmed that Belgium will take part in France's advanced nuclear-deterrence concept, one of eight European partners named by Macron: an ad hoc cooperation with no concrete investment, giving Belgium know-how and protection under the French umbrella, alongside US nuclear sharing.

relations_from.summary: At the Benelux summit at Bourglinster on 10 Sep 2025 the Belgian, Dutch and Luxembourg prime ministers signed a joint declaration reaffirming defence cooperation through the Benelux Steering Group and their role as founding NATO allies.

relations_from.summary: At the Ankara summit (July 2026) Belgium committed to keep defence spending at 2% of GDP until 2029 and to draw up a roadmap toward the Hague target of 3.5% of GDP core defence by 2035; NATO expects 2% in 2026 for the second year running. Government calculations including 'resilience' reach about 3.4% (2.01% direct plus 1.43%), figures not published officially.

sources.title: Belgium to keep defence spending at 2% of GDP till 2029
Belgium spends nearly 3.5% on defence, new estimates show

relations_from.summary: Strategic Vision 2025, approved by the government on 18 Jul 2025: defence at 2% (EUR 12.8bn) in 2025 rising to EUR 21.3bn in 2034, EUR 34.8bn of capacity commitments for 2026-34, 11 more F-35s, 10 NASAMS systems, a third ASW frigate, a third MQ-9B and 34,500 personnel by 2034.

sources.title: Belgium to add F-35s, spend billions on anti-air in defense catch-up

relations_from.summary: On 2 Sep 2025 Foreign Minister Prevot announced 12 measures: entry bans on two Israeli ministers, on violent settlers and on Hamas leaders, a ban on imports from the settlements, a review of public procurement with Israeli companies, limits on consular aid to Belgians in settlements and tighter arms transit rules. Cabinet approval of the settlement-goods ban followed in July 2026 (a draft royal decree on 18 Jul with a 120-day transition); Prevot called the Commission's own proposal a 'token gesture'.

sources.title: Cabinet decision on Palestinian sovereignty and measures on Israel

relations_from.summary: Belgium announced on 2 Sep 2025 that it would recognise Palestine at the UN General Assembly and signed the New York Declaration; the formal recognition by royal decree is conditional on the release of the last hostage and the exclusion of Hamas from governing Palestine, with diplomatic relations only after demilitarisation and elections. No decree reported by Oct 2026 (the recognition dataset still carries a non-recognition row); a Jul 2026 report that Belgium began drafting the procedure rests on a single Azerbaijani outlet.

relations_from.summary: On 17 Mar 2025 Rwanda cut diplomatic relations with Belgium and gave its diplomats 48 hours to leave, citing 'neo-colonial delusions', weeks after Belgium suspended aid and led calls for EU sanctions over the M23; the two countries expelled each other's diplomats.

relations_from.summary: On 22 Sep 2026, at the UN General Assembly, Prevot and his Rwandan counterpart Nduhungirehe announced the resumption of diplomatic relations after 18 months, thanking Qatar for facilitating a first meeting in June 2025; embassies to reopen soon, a chargé d'affaires first; Prevot said Belgium keeps defending the DRC's territorial integrity.

relations_from.summary: On 17 Mar 2026 a Brussels court ruled that Etienne Davignon, the last surviving Belgian official named, will stand trial over the 1961 killing of Patrice Lumumba; the trial is expected in 2027, a landmark for the colonial past.

sources.title: Landmark trial for Belgian colonial crimes to go ahead

relations_from.summary: New Belgian-Burundian cooperation programme of EUR 75m for 2024-28 (health, education, agriculture, climate, governance), implemented by Enabel, the first since 2015; Belgium's foreign ministry names Burundi its main bilateral development partner.

relations_from.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Prime Minister De Wever in Brussels on 1 Jul 2025 ahead of the EU-China summit; De Wever reaffirmed the one-China policy, Wang asked for a fair, predictable business environment for Chinese investors. Prevot later travelled to Hong Kong, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing for the 55th anniversary of relations.

relations_from.summary: On 13 Mar 2025 Belgian police searched 21 addresses in Brussels, Flanders and Wallonia (and one in Portugal) in a bribery probe of lobbying in the European Parliament that prosecutors said benefited Huawei; four people were charged with active corruption and criminal organisation. The probe started with a tip from the Belgian secret service; no foreign-interference charge.
